title: Pharmacy technicians in medication reconciliation at care transitions: a scoping review
abstract: Objective: to map what is known about pharmacy technicians performing medication reconciliation at admission, transfer and discharge. Design: scoping review following JBI guidance, reported with PRISMA-ScR. Sources: three bibliographic databases and professional and regulatory websites, English, from 2000. Results will be charted by task, supervision, measures, outcomes and scope.
introduction: Technicians take accurate admission histories in many hospitals, but their role at discharge, how they are supervised and what regulators allow are scattered across settings and jurisdictions.
methods: Searches were run by the hospital library; screening and charting used a form tested on the first seven retrieved records. The first recorded search returned no records and the second returned seven, both reported. Items not reported in sources were charted as not reported.
results: No charting has been done yet. The report will present the PRISMA-ScR flow diagram, an evidence map of tasks by transition, supervision models, outcome definitions and a scope table by jurisdiction.
discussion: The discussion will set out what the map means for the committee's decision on discharge reconciliation and where regulation, not evidence, is the limit.
limitations: English only; possible single-reviewer screening; grey literature may be incomplete.
conclusion: To be written after charting; it will describe the field and will not estimate effects.
summary: PRISMA-ScR-structured draft with results left empty until charting is done.
